    <RuleGroup name="" groupRelation="or">
      <!-- IOC: wiseman.EXE -->
      <ProcessCreate onmatch="include">
        <Image condition="end with">wiseman.exe</Image>
        <Hashes condition="is">ebba8f4342b65faccdd2a48be9f2654d3fa523360f17ff68d5498a453f76c205</Hashes>

      <!-- IOC: wininet.dll -->

      </ProcessCreate>

      <!-- T1033 – System Owner/User Discovery -->
      <ProcessCreate onmatch="include">
        <Image condition="end with">whoami.exe</Image>

      <ProcessCreate onmatch="include">

      </ProcessCreate>
      <ProcessCreate onmatch="include">

        <Image condition="is any">mstsc.exe;rdpclip.exe;ssh.exe;psexec.exe</Image>
      </ProcessCreate>

      <ProcessCreate onmatch="include">
        <Image condition="end with">reg.exe</Image>
        <CommandLine condition="contains any">add;delete;save</CommandLine>
      </ProcessCreate>

      <!-- T1016 – System Network Configuration Discovery -->
      <ProcessCreate onmatch="include">
        <Image condition="is any">ipconfig.exe;netsh.exe;route.exe;arp.exe</Image>
      </ProcessCreate>

[BEHAVIOR] Monitor processes that open **C:\Windows\System32\winlogon.exe** *or* **C:\Windows\System32\osk.exe** with **GrantedAccess** including `PROCESS_VM_READ|PROCESS_VM_WRITE|PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD`; the **CallTrace** should contain `user32.dll!SetWindowsHookEx` or similar hooking APIs → Source: T1056.001  

[IOC] Monitor when the executable **wiseman.EXE** (SourceImage) opens any target process with **GrantedAccess** set to a high‑privilege mask (e.g., `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS`); capture the **CallTrace** for the OpenProcess call → Source: wiseman.EXE  

*Omitted indicators:*  
- **wininet.dll** is a DLL module, not a process; Sysmon EventID 10 records only process‑to‑process accesses, so it cannot be observed with this event.  
- **T1140 (Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information)** describes file‑or‑command‑based decoding activity, which does not involve opening one process from another, and therefore cannot be captured by EventID 10.

<Sysmon schemaversion="4.60">
  <EventFiltering>
    <RuleGroup name="" groupRelation="or">
      <ProcessAccess onmatch="include">
        <!-- Credential dumping / token manipulation: access to LSASS -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <TargetImage condition="is">C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1F1FFF;0x1010;0x143A</GrantedAccess>
        </Rule>

        <!-- Keylogging / hooking: access to Winlogon or OSK with hooking APIs -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <TargetImage condition="is">C:\Windows\System32\winlogon.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1F1FFF;0x1010;0x143A</GrantedAccess>
          <CallTrace condition="contains any">advapi32.dll!OpenProcess;ntdll.dll!NtOpenProcess</CallTrace>
        </Rule>
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <TargetImage condition="is">C:\Windows\System32\osk.exe</TargetImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1F1FFF;0x1010;0x143A</GrantedAccess>
          <CallTrace condition="contains any">advapi32.dll!OpenProcess;ntdll.dll!NtOpenProcess</CallTrace>
        </Rule>

        <!-- IOC: suspicious source executable wiseman.EXE opening any process with high‑privilege access -->
        <Rule groupRelation="and">
          <SourceImage condition="image">wiseman.EXE</SourceImage>
          <GrantedAccess condition="contains any">0x1FFFFF;0x1F1FFF;0x1010;0x143A</GrantedAccess>
        </Rule>
      </ProcessAccess>
    </RuleGroup>
  </EventFiltering>
</Sysmon>

**Omitted attack patterns and why they were not included**

- **T1082 (System Information Discovery)** – This technique is focused on reading system information; it does not involve writing registry values, so it cannot be observed with Sysmon Event ID 13 (SetValue).  
- **T1012 (Query Registry)** – Similarly, this technique involves reading registry data, not modifying it, and therefore is outside the scope of Event ID 13.  
- **T1056.001 (Keylogging)** – The primary behavior described for keylogging is API hooking and direct keystroke capture. While a keylogger may later use persistence mechanisms (covered under T1547.001), the technique itself does not explicitly mandate registry value writes of DWORD/QWORD type, so no dedicated SetValue monitoring rule was added beyond the generic persistence keys already covered.  

No other indicators of compromise or vulnerability‑specific registry paths were provided, so no additional recommendations could be justified.
